rationale: Cheapest acceptable model for Week 1 scope: a bounded single-turn Q&A endpoint whose deliverable is a working /ask contract with observable tokens_used/cost_usd, not answer quality tuned across models. Dev and MVP-proofing queries at this stage don't require an edge/flagship model. gpt-4.1-nano is cheaper than the prior selection (gpt-4o-mini) on both input ($0.10 vs $0.15 per 1M) and output ($0.40 vs $0.60 per 1M), and unlike several newer nano/mini models it has exactly one unambiguous 'standard'-tier pricing record in config/model-pricing.json. Revisit once VERA-DAR's evidence-context pipeline (Session 2+) makes response quality, not just cost, a load-bearing evaluation dimension.
notes: 2026-09-13: switched from gpt-4o-mini. Deliberately did NOT pick gpt-5-nano (cheaper still, $0.025-0.05 input / $0.20-0.40 output) because it -- like gpt-5.4-nano and gpt-5-mini -- has both a 'standard' and a 'flex' pricing record sharing the same effective_from date, and vera.pricing.config.latest_pricing_for() ignores service_tier when picking the latest record. Since vera/ask_service.py never requests OpenAI's flex processing tier, that lookup could silently report the cheaper flex price for a model actually billed at the standard rate. Fixing latest_pricing_for to be tier-aware (like scripts/refresh_openai_pricing.py's own latest_for_model_and_tier helper) is a separate, not-yet-made decision from this file's model choice. Earlier (2026-09-12) finding about gpt-4o-mini's catalog-page absence is now moot since it's no longer selected.
